text: Atorvastatin acts as a potent, competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR), the rate-limiting enzyme in the mevalonate pathway responsible for endogenous cholesterol biosynthesis. By binding to the active site of HMGCR, atorvastatin prevents the conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate, thereby reducing intracellular cholesterol levels and triggering the upregulation of LDL receptors to clear circulating cholesterol. This mechanism is well-documented and serves as the primary therapeutic basis for managing hypercholesterolemia.
